standards_backbone: ISO 4406:2021 (oil cleanliness; current edition, supersedes the 2017 edition cited in research/domain/04)
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC but physics-grounded. All numeric values are representative industry estimates derived from the cited standards and research briefs (machinery/17-20, domain/04-08). Site-specific baseline calibration is mandatory before any production deployment. No proprietary Tata Steel data is used.
currency_note: INR/USD figures use approx 1 USD = INR 83.5. Cost ranges are per-event business-impact estimates from research/machinery/20 (OxMaint, FeroLabs, ifactory, Tata Steel AR 2024-25).

generation_contract.note: The failure_scenario_catalog is a TEMPLATE set (12 FAILURE archetypes + 36 NORMAL archetypes = 25% catalog-level proportion). This 25% is a scenario-design ratio for coverage, NOT the row-level label distribution. The generator MUST NOT propagate the catalog proportion to rows.
generation_contract.target_failure_rate_note: Final row-level failure rate must land in 0.5-5% (sweet spot per research/domain/08 Dimension 4; the DOMAIN_IMBALANCE_OVERRIDE band 0.5-5% scores 'ok' / 90+). 15-40% trips the 'warning / over-collected' rule; >40% is 'unrealistic / synthetic'.
generation_contract.expansion_rule: Each NORMAL scenario expands into a long healthy timeseries (steady-state timesteps). Each FAILURE scenario contributes ONLY the degradation->failure window (a small fraction of its asset's total timeline) plus its preceding healthy run-to-failure (RTF) trajectory. Healthy timesteps vastly outnumber degraded/failure timesteps so the aggregate FAILURE-labelled row fraction lands inside target_failure_rate.
generation_contract.rtf_requirement: Each FAILURE scenario must emit a complete healthy->degraded->failure RTF trajectory (per research/domain/08 Dimension 3) so RUL regression is feasible; no truncation of the degradation curve.
generation_contract.min_failure_events_note: Aggregate FAILURE instances should be >=100 across the dataset (research/domain/08 Dimension 2: <30 critical, 30-100 warning, >100 ok), achieved by repeating each FAILURE archetype across multiple synthetic episodes while keeping the overall row-level rate within target_failure_rate.

sensors.note: MFL is the LMA proxy. Warning 150 mV ~= 8-12% LMA (advisory). Alarm 300 mV ~= >15-20% LMA / >=12 random broken wires in one lay length (>=4 in one strand) = discard per ISO 4309. Diameter-reduction discard is -7% (warning -3%); LMA-percentage and broken-wire-count are distinct metrics and must not be conflated.

degradation_timeline.warning: AE crosses warn (6 dBuV) weeks 6-8 (no vib change yet)
degradation_timeline.alarm: AE reaches ~8 dBuV (warning-exceeded, below AE alarm 12) + envelope BPFO 1.0->3.0g + temp drift, weeks 8-10

JSR.HR.STD3.WR.BRG01.AE.RMS.note: 8 dBuV is between AE warn (6) and AE alarm (12) = warning-exceeded / stage-2 onset, not the earliest stage-1 indicator. AE is the leading indicator (crosses warn ~weeks 6-8 before any vibration change).

failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Subsurface rolling-contact fatigue initiating outer-race spall (ISO 15243 fatigue); accelerated by lube contamination.
correct_resolution: Controlled stop (Zone D / temp>100C), no emergency trip
Hydraulic bearing puller; never strike bearing
Inspect journal vs OEM H7/k6, regrind if worn

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE

degradation_timeline.warning: cepstrum rahmonics rise + GMF sidebands, weeks 8-10

failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Tooth-root fatigue crack from prior high-torque cobble event; chunky spall debris.
correct_resolution: Remove gearbox via crane to repair bay
Replace gear wheel + bearings; set backlash 0.1-0.3mm

cost_impact.note: Point estimate raised into the cited range. Per research/machinery/20 sec2F, HSM gearbox failure production loss during a 5-21 day swap is $500k-$3M (OxMaint hot strip mill gearbox case); $600k reflects a ~7-day swap of the custom large-module gear wheel (36-week lead spare) plus secondary-damage repair. Prior $300k point estimate was below its own range floor and unsupported.

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE
failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Rotor bar fracture from repeated high-torque starts / thermal cycling; sidebands at (1-2s)f1.
correct_resolution: Confirm via MCSA at steady load (sideband >-35dBc)
Plan motor swap within 2-4 weeks (insurance spare)
Send failed motor for rotor bar test + repair
Verify phase rotation before energising spare

cost_impact.note: Figure is rewind+swap LABOUR + lost-production cost only (planned 10h swap to standby + crane + alignment). The MTR-MV-6000 insurance spare ($450k / INR 37.575M, 40-week lead) is a REUSABLE rotating capital asset, NOT consumed: the failed motor is sent for rotor-bar repair/rewind (RWND-KIT-MV ~$15k) and returned to spare stock, so it is not expensed against this event. No double-counting of the $450k motor capital here.

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE

correct_resolution: Install new SiC/SiC seal, faces fingerprint-free

correct_resolution: Reduce casting speed if in liquid-core zone
End heat, cool strand 2-4h before bay entry
Replace seized roll + bearings, clean nozzles
Set segment gap per slab format, pressure-test

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE

degradation_timeline.warning: TC delta 20->25C + friction spike + level wave (need all 3)

failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Shell sticking to mould wall (poor lubrication / improper taper / SEN blockage); confirmed by 3-sensor agreement (single sensor >40% FAR).
correct_resolution: BPS alarm: reduce casting speed to minimum 0.5 m/min immediately
If escalating: full emergency stop (stop withdrawal + close tundish gate)
Do not operate until steel solidified 4-6h+
Post-breakout: remove skull, replace damaged segments, 5-whys RCA within 48h

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE
failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Subsurface roll defect activated by cobble/thermal shock; spall printing on strip at period = piD.
correct_resolution: Stop rolling on spall-printed product, segregate strip
Send roll to roll shop: grind 3-5mm below spall
UT test after grind; condemn if below min dia

failure_scenario_catalog.label: FAILURE
failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Dry/failed idler bearing; seized idler under loaded belt is #1 belt-fire initiator.

cost_impact.note: Direct repair cost of a single seized-idler event caught before fire propagation (idler swap + short belt repair), reconciled at 1 USD = INR 83.5. The 'Bhilai 2019 Rs 1 Cr' framing from research/machinery/20 is dropped because its INR (Rs 1 Cr) and USD ($7,500) do not reconcile at any plausible FX rate (Rs 1 Cr ~= $120k); a full conveyor-fire loss would be ~INR 10,000,000 / ~USD 120,000 and is NOT what this idler-caught-early scenario represents.

correct_resolution: Automatic fuel cutoff at <40% flame signal

degradation_timeline.alarm: MFL 300mV (>15-20% LMA) / >=12 random broken wires in 1 lay (or >=4 in one strand) / dia -7%

failure_scenario_catalog.root_cause: Wire-rope fatigue / broken wires exceeding ISO 4309 discard criteria: >=12 random broken wires in one lay length (or >=4 in one strand), and/or MRT LMA >15-20%, and/or rope-diameter reduction >-7% nominal.
correct_resolution: Take crane out of service immediately (do not lift)
If load suspended: lower under control first
Replace rope; inspect drum/sheave grooves; fleet angle <4deg
